Aortic stenosis
Aortic stenosis is a narrowing of the aortic valve, which is the valve that separates the left ventricle from the aorta. The narrowing of the valve causes the heart to work harder to pump blood through the body. The heart's response to the increased workload is to thicken the walls of the left ventricle. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is a condition in which the heart is thickened. The thickening is caused by the heart muscle becoming larger than normal. This can happen for many reasons, but it is most often caused by a mutation in the genes that control heart muscle growth.
